R1.title: NIAID - Immune System Overview
R1.receipt: Bone marrow origins; maturation in the upper-chest thymus; lymphatic meeting sites.

R2.title: NIAID - Immune Cells
R2.receipt: T/B roles, CD4/CD8 recognition, MHC presentation, cytokines, apoptosis, and regulation.

R3.title: Immunobiology - Selection of lymphocytes
R3.receipt: Peptide-MHC recognition and positive/negative thymic selection; foundational 2001 reference.

R4.title: NIAID - Immune Tolerance
R4.receipt: Autoreactive cells can remain despite developmental selection; additional tolerance mechanisms.

R5.title: Immunobiology - The course of the adaptive response
R5.receipt: Dendritic-cell migration, innate context, co-stimulation, and selective expansion.

R6.title: Immunobiology - Immunological memory
R6.receipt: Response contraction, persistent memory, faster recall, and B-derived plasma cells.

R7.title: NIH - Immune response improves after vaccination
R7.receipt: A specific vaccination example engaging T and B cells; not a universal duration estimate.

R8.title: NIH - Vaccine immune responses to Omicron
R8.receipt: Cellular responses can remain relevant despite breakthrough infection; no infection-proof claim.

R9.title: NIH HIVinfo - HIV and AIDS: The Basics
R9.receipt: HIV attacks CD4 cells and compromises immune defenses.

R10.title: NCI - Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors
R10.receipt: Checkpoint restraint, therapeutic blockade, and possible inflammatory side effects.

R11.title: NCI - T-cell Transfer Therapy
R11.receipt: Engineered receptors can bind selected surface proteins; restricted applications and serious risks.

R12.title: NCI - Immunotherapy to Treat Cancer
R12.receipt: Patient responses vary, resistance exists, and healthy tissues can be affected.

R13.title: Immunobiology - Vaccination
R13.receipt: Protective requirements and T-cell involvement vary among pathogens and vaccines.
